name: Battle of Crécy
note: The English face south east; the plan puts them at the top, looking down the slope at the French. The accounts do not give the exact places of the pits, of the archers on the flanks, or of the French battles behind the first two, so these are placed by judgement. The accounts do not say which French battle made the later charges; the plan gives them to the battle of Lorraine and Blois, then to Philip's rearguard. Accounts differ on the numbers on both sides.

terrain.name: Hillside
terrain.quote: facing south east on a sloping hillside, broken by copses and terracing

terrain.name: Wadicourt
terrain.quote: The left flank was anchored against Wadicourt

terrain.name: Crécy
terrain.quote: the right was protected by Crécy itself and the River Maye beyond

terrain.name: River Maye
terrain.quote: the right was protected by Crécy itself and the River Maye beyond

terrain.name: Pits
terrain.quote: the English dug pits in front of their positions, intended to disorder attacking cavalry

units.name: English vanguard
units.quote: commanded the vanguard with 800 men-at-arms, 2,000 archers and 1,000 foot soldiers including Welsh spearmen

units.name: English left battle
units.quote: the other battle was led by the Earl of Arundel, with 800 men-at-arms and 1,200 archers

units.name: English reserve battle
units.quote: Behind them, the King commanded the reserve battle, with 700 men-at-arms and 2,000 archers.

units.name: Longbowmen, vanguard
units.quote: with longbowmen on each flank and in a skirmish line to their front

units.name: Longbowmen, left battle
units.quote: with longbowmen on each flank and in a skirmish line to their front

units.name: Detachment from the reserve
units.quote: Edward sent forward a detachment from his reserve battle to rescue the situation.

units.name: Genoese crossbowmen
units.quote: The crossbowmen, under Antonio Doria and Carlo Grimaldi, formed the French vanguard.

units.name: Alençon's mounted battle
units.quote: a large battle of mounted men-at-arms led by Count Charles of Alençon

units.name: Battle of Lorraine and Blois
units.quote: The next battle was led by Duke Rudolph of Lorraine and Count Louis of Blois

phases.title: The English hold the hillside
phases.text: Edward's army stood in three battles on a slope, with pits dug in front. French scouts came in sight of them from Abbeville, and the French column followed with the Genoese crossbowmen in front.
phases.quote: Around noon on 26 August French scouts, advancing north from Abbeville, came in sight of the English.

phases.title: The archery duel
phases.text: The Genoese went forward and shot at the English longbowmen. The longbowmen outranged them and shot more than three times as fast, and the crossbowmen had no pavises, which were still with the French baggage.
phases.quote: The Genoese engaged the English longbowmen in an archery duel.

phases.title: The Genoese flee through their own cavalry
phases.text: The Italians were quickly defeated and fled. Knights in Alençon's division, hampered by the routed mercenaries, hacked at them as they retreated, and the clash threw the leading battle into disarray.
phases.quote: The knights and nobles following in Alençon's division, hampered by the routed mercenaries, hacked at them as they retreated.

phases.title: Alençon's charge uphill
phases.text: Alençon's battle charged, disordered by its hurried start, the fleeing Italians, the mud, the slope and the pits. Archers shot the unarmoured horses, and the charge had lost much of its force when it reached the English men-at-arms.
phases.quote: Alençon's battle (division of the army) then launched a cavalry charge.

phases.title: The first charge is beaten off
phases.text: The English men-at-arms and spearmen received a charge that had lost much of its force, and the hand-to-hand fighting that followed was fierce. Alençon was among those killed, and the French attack was beaten off.
phases.quote: Alençon was among those killed. The French attack was beaten off.

phases.title: Fresh French cavalry repeat the charge
phases.text: A fresh body of French cavalry moved up to the foot of the hill and charged over ground littered with dead and wounded men and horses. They were too disordered to break into the English formation, and a long mêlée followed.
phases.quote: Fresh forces of French cavalry moved into position at the foot of the hill and repeated Alençon's charge.

phases.title: Edward sends a detachment from the reserve
phases.text: With the Prince of Wales hard pressed, Edward sent forward a detachment from his reserve battle to rescue the situation, and the French were repulsed again.
phases.quote: Edward sent forward a detachment from his reserve battle to rescue the situation.

phases.title: The charges go on into the night
phases.text: The French repeated their charges late into the night, each ending in fierce fighting and a French retreat. The English ranks were thinned, but men from the rear stepped forward to fill the gaps.
phases.quote: How many times the French charged is disputed, but they continued late into the night

phases.title: Philip leaves the field
phases.text: Philip was caught up in the fighting, had two horses killed under him and was hit by an arrow in the jaw. He left the field, though it is unclear why, and near midnight most of the French army melted away.
phases.quote: Finally, Philip abandoned the field of battle, although it is unclear why.
